Title: Is refacing cheaper than replacing cabinets?
Description: Usually, yes. Guides say refacing costs 30–50% less than replacing, or about half. Against stock cabinets the gap can close or reverse on the cabinet line alone, but replacement adds removal, countertop and wall costs that refacing avoids. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do Command strips damage walls?
Description: Usually not when used as directed, but they can. The sources tie damage to pulling strips off the wrong way, freshly painted or textured walls, and overloading. 3M says pull the tab slowly straight down and wait 7 days after painting. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is it cheaper to paint a small bathroom?
Description: In total dollars yes, per square foot rarely. A powder room is often $150–$400 for a pro, but minimum charges of $150 to $500 push the per-square-foot price up. DIY is cheap because one gallon covers a small room. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How long does it take to paint a bedroom?
Description: Professionals commonly finish a standard bedroom in one to two days including prep. A first-time DIYer should plan for about a weekend, because furniture moving, taping and drying between coats take longer than the painting itself. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much does it cost per square foot to paint a living room?
Description: Labor runs about $1.50–$3 per sq ft of wall in some guides and $2–$6 in others. Fixr gives $1.50–$3.50 for walls and $3–$4 per sq ft for the whole room including ceiling and trim. Your area and the scope of work decide where in that spread you land. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is painting cheaper than replacing cabinets?
Description: Yes. One painting company says painting saves 60–80% compared with a full replacement priced at $15,000–$30,000 or more. That figure comes from a contractor, not a neutral study. Our refacing vs. repainting vs. replacing guide compares all three side by side. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is contact paper the same as peel-and-stick countertop film?
Description: The terms overlap. SlabWise separates thin contact paper ($0.20 to $0.80 per sq ft) from thicker vinyl ($1 to $3) and recommends at least 6 mil for vinyl. Product pages often use the names interchangeably, so check thickness and the maker's heat statement. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can a renter install built-in shelves?
Description: Only with the landlord's approval, ideally in writing. The shelves stay behind, and damage beyond small holes can come out of your deposit. Builds and Buys steers renters toward freestanding furniture. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can a landlord keep my deposit for nail holes?
Description: It depends on how many and how big. FindLaw treats non-excessive nail holes as normal wear and tear, and another guide lists small picture-hanging holes as ordinary. Large or numerous holes are more likely to count as damage. Check your lease and state rules before patching or painting. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much cash do I need to move into an apartment?
Description: One 2026 guide says usually two to four times monthly rent, once you add the first month, a one-to-two-month deposit, fees, moving and setup. An August 2026 example for $1,400 rent reached $6,450 with a $2,000 cushion. Your lease and moving method change this a lot. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much does move-out cleaning cost?
Description: Most guides land between $100 and $500 for an apartment and up to $750 or more for a three-bedroom house. The exact figure depends on size, condition and whether oven, fridge and carpet are included. Get two or three written quotes with the scope spelled out before you book. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much does it cost to organize a small closet without drilling?
Description: A pocket or hook organizer is about $10–$40, and a freestanding rack like IKEA's MULIG is $9.99 with a 44 lb limit. Tension rods work for light loads. For most small closets, tens of dollars covers it. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is a paint sprayer worth it for interior painting?
Description: Usually not for one furnished room: masking takes longer than rolling and the sprayer uses more paint. It is more likely to pay off in empty spaces, across several rooms, on textured ceilings, or for cabinets and trim where a smooth finish matters. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can I use peel-and-stick behind a stove?
Description: Sources split. Family Handyman says no, Bob Vila says most are fine if the literature says so, and manufacturers that publish numbers give 6 to 8 inches of clearance and a 120–140°F ceiling. If your product lists no heat rating, keep it away from burners. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is peel-and-stick wallpaper cheaper than paint?
Description: Not usually. Our estimate for a 96 sq ft accent wall is $18–$96 for a gallon of paint against about $100–$225 for mainstream peel-and-stick rolls. Paint stays cheaper for a full room. Wallpaper's case is reversibility, not price. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How many rolls of peel-and-stick wallpaper do I need for a bedroom?
Description: For a 12×12 ft room with 8 ft ceilings and 28 sq ft single rolls, our arithmetic gives about 15 rolls if the pattern needs no matching and about 29 with a 12-inch repeat. Area math alone says 14. Add the extra roll sellers suggest for lot differences. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Are wall decals cheaper than peel-and-stick wallpaper?
Description: For a small accent, yes: a WallPops set is around $21. For a full 96 sq ft wall, no: wallpaper rolls come to roughly $104 to $240 in our estimate, against near $690 in decal sheets. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: What is the cheapest way to cover an ugly rental floor?
Description: A rug and pad, at about $27 to $214 for a 5x7 set in September 2026 listings, is cheapest but covers only part of a room. For full coverage, peel-and-stick tile and foam tiles start around $0.70 to $0.85 per sq ft, though peel-and-stick carries the most residue risk. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can a landlord charge me for small nail holes?
Description: In the sources we read, small nail holes from pictures are normal wear and tear and cannot be deducted. Large holes, clusters of holes and holes that crack the paint can be. State law varies, so check yours and photograph the walls at move-in. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much does under-cabinet lighting cost for a whole kitchen?
Description: For a 10-foot run, plug-in kits come to about $20–$110 in 2026 listings (our estimate), and hardwired jobs $250–$800 across the recent guides. One 2023 guide implies $1,500–$2,500 for six to eight separately installed lights, so ask for an itemized quote that lists the fixture count. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is refacing worth it compared with painting?
Description: It is worth it if the door style bothers you or the doors are worn. Painting changes only color and costs a fraction of refacing. If the style is acceptable and the boxes are sound, painting delivers most of the visual change for far less. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Are Command strips safe for a mirror?
Description: Only within the rating, frame size and pair count on the pack. 3M's chart tops out at 16 lb and a 24×36 in frame for four large pairs. Do not hang a mirror over a bed, and use anchors for a heavy or valuable one. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do I need special paint for a bathroom?
Description: Guides recommend mildew-resistant acrylic or latex paint, usually in satin or semi-gloss. The premium is about $10–$20 per gallon in one guide, small on a one-gallon job. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do I need primer?
Description: Primer helps when you are covering a dark color with a light one, painting over stains or bare patched drywall, or changing between very different finishes. If the walls are in good shape and you are staying in the same color family, you can often skip it. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How many gallons of paint does a living room need?
Description: Most living rooms need 2 to 4 gallons for two coats of walls. Our 16×14 example needs 3, and an open plan of 20×30 ft needs 4–5. Add a gallon or two if you paint the ceiling. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do I have to sand kitchen cabinets before painting?
Description: Mostly yes. Benjamin Moore's data sheet asks for roughening cabinetry with 220-grit or coarser before priming, and Family Handyman suggests a 120-grit scuff on previously painted doors. Degrease first, since grease clogs sandpaper. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can I put a hot pan on countertop film?
Description: No. Sources agree on trivets even where products carry a heat rating. Quoted ratings are 150–175°F, including d-c-fix's 170°F, and one guide says damage begins near 275–325°F. A pan fresh off a burner can pass any of those numbers, so use a trivet every time. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do freestanding bookcases need to be anchored to the wall?
Description: The CPSC recommends it for bookcases and dressers. Use screws long enough to reach a wood stud and metal brackets; the National Council on Aging says a kit costs under $20 and takes about 20 minutes. Anchoring to drywall alone is much weaker. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: What if my landlord misses the deadline?
Description: It depends on the state. New York's Attorney General says a landlord who misses the 14-day itemized receipt deadline must return the whole deposit. Washington's statute says the landlord cannot assert claims to keep it. Read your own state's rule. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do I really need renters insurance?
Description: Your landlord's policy does not cover your belongings, per the NAIC and New York's regulator. NerdWallet puts the U.S. average at $151 a year as of January 2026; other guides say $15 to $30 a month. Check your lease for any requirement and compare quotes with identical limits. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How long does a professional move-out clean take?
Description: Vendor pages give about 1.5–5 hours for a studio or one-bedroom and 2–8 hours for a two-bedroom, a wide spread that the pages do not explain. Heavy soiling, extra crew members or add-ons like carpet and windows change the time, so ask the company how many people it sends and how long it expects to be there. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Is an over-door organizer worth it?
Description: Yes for shoes, accessories and cleaning supplies, at roughly $0.83–$1.63 per pocket by our math. No for hanging clothes, since it adds no rod space. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much does it cost to rent a paint sprayer?
Description: Recent guides put airless sprayers at about $85–$103 a day and $412–$500 a week, though one 2026 guide lists $40–$110 a day. Add a possible deposit, a damage waiver, and up to about $100 for a dirty return. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How long does peel-and-stick last?
Description: Sources range from 1 to 2 years for budget products to 5 to 20 for good ones on well-prepped walls. About 3 to 10 years is the middle. Heat, moisture and poor prep shorten it. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Will peel-and-stick wallpaper damage my walls?
Description: On smooth, cured satin or eggshell paint, manufacturers say it removes cleanly. Flat, matte, textured, freshly painted or non-stick paint raises the chance of lifting paint. Every source we read is a seller or publisher, so test a small area first. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: How much does it cost to wallpaper one accent wall?
Description: A 12×8 ft wall is about $100–$180 in mainstream rolls when there is no repeat to match, and $200–$360 with a 12-inch repeat. Designer double rolls raise that to $120–$450, and custom-cut is about $479 at $4.99 per square foot. Labor is extra. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Are wall stickers better than wallpaper for renters?
Description: Neither is clearly safer. Sellers say both remove cleanly from smooth, cured paint, and the wall finish matters more than the product. Decals cost less to try and bond a smaller area (our inference); wallpaper gives a finished look. Get written permission either way. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can I put peel-and-stick tile over hardwood?
Description: The manufacturer instructions we read list hardwood, carpet and floating floors as unsuitable, and say installing over an existing covering releases the maker from responsibility. They also require primer on the surface. Skip it unless your landlord approves the change in writing. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Do I need permission for peel-and-stick products?
Description: Check your lease. A 2026 tenant guide lists adhesive wallpaper among alterations that generally need consent. Hooks and rugs rarely raise the question, but a short email costs nothing and gives you a record. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.

Title: Can renters install under-cabinet lights?
Description: Yes, if they choose plug-in or battery lights that mount with adhesive, clips or magnets. Hardwiring changes the electrical system, so it needs the landlord's written approval, and sources say a licensed electrician should do it. Check your lease before adding anything permanent. Full guide with sources at thebudgethomefixes.com.
